artifact.target_user: Independent recruiter or boutique-search operator doing relationship-dense work on a Mac

score_basis.method: Atomic manifest weights only. Passing requirements earn full weight. Unproven requirements earn zero. No averaging or partial credit.

requirement_results.finding: The frozen lifecycle evidence still proves the required Mac process boundary: closing the main window leaves the menu-bar process alive, and explicit quit terminates the process. Build 7 does not change the lifecycle control path.

Build 7 native live readback and canonical receipt readback use the shared task and receipt contracts with stable IDs, revisions, and empty external effects. The earlier cross-surface proof still establishes that the same canonical task survives Web readback, and the build 7 delta changes the first-response wording rather than the shared task or receipt contract shape.

The native shell remains a typed boundary. The frozen source audit shows no embedded renderer bridge, no arbitrary native tool handoff, and no widened system authority. Build 7 changes do not add a new capability path outside the typed allowlist.

The local recovery boundary remains account-scoped and fail-closed on sign-out. Earlier runtime proof still shows relaunch does not reopen prior task context, and build 7 adds a separate encrypted unknown-operation store that is cleared on sign-out and restored only when the authenticated workspace, account, pursuit, person, and relationship scope match exactly.

The Quick Panel still starts empty with no implicit capture, clipboard read, or window read, and explicit capture still creates one visible local item with a receipt. Build 7 does not change the capture-intake boundary.

The build 7 live suite directly proves immutable manifest separation: after editing submitted context, the later manifest produces a different capture, task, and run, while the original run keeps only its original evidence IDs. The old run never absorbs later-added evidence.

TTL expiry and manual deletion still account for raw context and registered derivatives before and after relaunch. The build 7 source-delta audit explicitly marks the retention and derivative-lineage implementation byte-identical to build 6, so the destructive retention proofs remain admissible for build 7.

Run history remains reconstructable from canonical state. The build 7 live proposal test asserts that run audit readback includes evidence IDs, eligible capabilities, budget ceilings, and authorized source state, while the canonical task and proposal readbacks preserve the semantic snapshot digests and task revisions that pin the bounded context.

Later claim retrieval fails closed when evidence is revoked, deleted, or stale. Build 7 revoked-authority readback leaves the proposal back in review with no receipt, and the retained build 6 TTL and deletion proofs show empty evidence arrays, cancelled decision bundles, and stale or redacted tasks after relaunch.

Build 7 repairs the durable response-loss boundary. The source now encrypts and persists the original operation correlation before the decision POST leaves process memory, restores it only inside the same authenticated relationship scope, reconciles by operation GET, prevents a second POST, and clears durable state only after verified receipt or terminal conflict. The live relaunch proof records exactly one review POST, one dropped response, four blocked GETs, zero action-completion POSTs, a relaunched reconcile of the same operation ID, and the verified canonical receipt.

Permission revocation after preview still blocks before any review write. The build 7 live test revokes source authority between preview and decision, the client revalidates evidence immediately before the consequential request, and the canonical readback shows no proposal receipt and no external effects.

The frozen build still excludes the prohibited macOS permission surface. The source audit shows no Accessibility, Automation, Input Monitoring, or Full Disk Access implementation path, `project.yml` still sets empty entitlements, and the focused privacy proof confirms there is still no system-notification sink linked into the build 7 binary.

The build 7 source and unit-test corpus still point in the right direction for optional local OCR loss: the image remains local, submission stays blocked, and the UI copy says no cloud fallback ran. I did not find a direct frozen runtime trace for that outage path in the build 7 evidence ledger, so I cannot honestly mark the requirement proven.

strengths.title: Response-loss recovery is now durable, scoped, and duplicate-safe
strengths.detail: The build 7 fix finally proves the key release-gate claim: the client persists the original decision correlation before POST, restores only the same authenticated scope after relaunch, reconciles by GET, and clears local recovery only after verified terminal receipt.

strengths.title: Retention and deletion remain auditable after restart
strengths.detail: The retained destructive proofs still show derivative lineage accounting, zero private-sentinel residue across 93 public tables, cancelled decision bundles, and empty run evidence after both TTL expiry and manual deletion, and the build 7 retention implementation is byte-identical to the proven build 6 paths.

strengths.title: The native shell still keeps authority narrow
strengths.detail: The frozen evidence continues to show a typed service boundary, no generic renderer bridge, no widened macOS permission surface, and no notification delivery sink capable of leaking candidate content.

issues.title: Optional local-model outage still lacks direct frozen runtime proof
issues.detail: I found source-level and unit-level evidence for the no-cloud-fallback OCR outage path, but not a dedicated runtime trace from the frozen build 7 ledger. That keeps `MAC-TX-013` at zero even though the surrounding implementation looks consistent with the intended privacy boundary.
issues.recommended_fix: Add one frozen build 7 runtime trace or focused live test artifact that exercises local OCR unavailability and records the exact fallback state, local-only retention, and absence of any cloud handoff.

summary: Technical experience passes at 95/100. All release-gate `MAC-TX-*` requirements are proven for build 7, including the repaired response-loss relaunch path. The only remaining gap is `MAC-TX-013`, which I am keeping unproven because the frozen ledger still lacks direct runtime evidence for the optional local-model outage path.
